posts.caption:
SPF 100 isn't twice as strong as SPF 50. 🧴

SPF 15 blocks about 93% of UVB, SPF 30 about 97%, SPF 50 about 98%, SPF 100 about 99%. Past 30, the real difference is how much you put on and how often you reapply.

The two-finger rule: two finger-lengths for face and neck, again every 2 hours outdoors.

Send this to the friend who uses a pea-sized drop 👀

Save this before your next routine. Patch test anything new, and if your skin is reactive, check with a dermatologist.

posts.caption:
Your skin barrier might be damaged. 🧱

3 signs: your moisturizer stings, your skin feels tight right after washing, or it's oily and flaky at the same time.

The fix: pause strong actives (retinoids, acids, scrubs) for 1–2 weeks, and keep it to a gentle cleanser + a moisturizer with ceramides. If irritation doesn't calm down, see a dermatologist.

Save this for the next time your skin acts up.

posts.caption:
That tiny open jar on your skincare isn't decoration. 🫙

It's the Period After Opening symbol: the number tells you how many months a product stays good once it's opened. 12M = 12 months, 6M = 6 months. Past that, it can lose strength or start to irritate.

Bonus: if your vitamin C serum has turned dark orange, it has oxidized. Replace it.

Save this and go check your shelf 👀

6 skin myths on trial. ⚖️ Most of us still believe at least two.

Oily skin still needs moisturizer. UVA comes through windows. Pores don't open or close. SPF 50 still needs reapplying. Price doesn't decide results. Water helps, but dry skin needs moisture from the outside too.

Which one did you believe? 👇 Send this to the friend who's still team "no moisturizer".

posts.caption:
At UV 3, your skin already needs SPF. ☀️

The UV index, decoded: 0–2 low (unless you burn easily), 3–5 moderate: SPF 30+ and shade around midday, 6–7 high: less sun between 10 am and 4 pm, 8+ very high: bare skin burns quickly.

The temperature tells you nothing about UV. Check the number before you skip sunscreen.

Source: US EPA UV Index scale. Save this and check today's UV 👀

posts.caption:
Your acne cream can bleach your pillowcase. 🚫

Benzoyl peroxide bleaches colored towels, pillowcases and even hair, so use white ones and let it dry first. Plus 3 more things your skincare should never meet: retinol and a face wax, lime juice and the sun, and the SPF 30 + SPF 30 = 60 myth.

Save this before you need it, and send it to the friend with the bleached towels 👀

Sources: AAD, MedlinePlus, Poison Control, Skin Cancer Foundation.

posts.caption:
One day is not a patch test. 🧪

Dermatologists recommend 7 to 10 days: a small dab on the inside of your elbow, your normal amount, twice a day. Redness, itching or swelling? Wash it off and stop. Nothing after 10 days? Now it can go on your face.

Source: American Academy of Dermatology. Save this before you open your next product.

posts.caption:
Your shower might be drying out your skin. 🚿

4 rules for dry skin season: 5 to 10 minutes, warm water not hot, pat dry instead of rubbing, and moisturize while your skin is still damp. Creams and ointments hold in more moisture than lotions.

Source: American Academy of Dermatology. Save this for the cold months.

posts.caption:
"Hypoallergenic" means whatever the brand wants. 🏷️

There's no federal standard for it in the US, so patch test anyway. 3 more label words, decoded: "broad spectrum" means UVA and UVB, "water resistant" can only mean 40 or 80 minutes, and a sunscreen with no date? Treat it as expired 3 years after purchase.

Save this for your next shop.

Sources: US FDA.
